checked.found: Extinction commonly dated to about 1000 CE (shell radiocarbon c. 1000 BP); some accounts of later survival are anecdotal.
Wikipedia: 'By 1445 C.E., all moa had become extinct', in under a century, nine species. Note Holdaway et al. 2014 centres on c. 1425 +/- 10, so 1445 is within the range.
Discovered 1741, last reportedly killed c. 1768 on Bering Island.
Last known pair killed on Eldey, Iceland, June 1844 (standard account; not re-searched).

1858 is the widely cited date for the last Cape lion killed (one source says Natal 1865, and the exact year is uncertain). But genetic work suggests the Cape lion was probably only the southern population of the southern African lion, so 'ending a distinct subspecies' is not supported.
Australian Species Profile and Threats database gives extinct c. 1865 (listed extinct 1997). Wikipedia infobox says 1851 and a captive bird lived to 1873, so the year is conventional, not exact.
Only native land mammal of the Falklands; last known killed 1876 at Shallow Bay, West Falkland.
Cats established on Stephens Island 1894; most specimens 1894-95, possibly a few to 1899 (Galbreath and Brown 2004). 1895 is a fair conventional date.
Last live specimens collected 1902 (Norman Criddle, Treesbank, Manitoba).
Last confirmed sighting 1907 (standard account; secondary source only).
Incas, last known specimen, died at Cincinnati Zoo in 1918.

Traditional account: last wild Barbary lion shot in the Atlas Mountains in 1922. Newer oral-history research claims survival to the 1940s-60s, and one source gives 1942, but 1922 is the standard date.
Booming Ben, last heath hen, on Martha's Vineyard; extinct 1932 (some say declared 1933).
eLife 2024 and most sources say last collected 1941 (California Insects 1980 says 1943).
Last confirmed sighting 1952 at Serranilla Bank; declared extinct 2008.

Wikipedia infobox says extinct 1970 and assessed extinct in 2003, but its text gives a 1998 sighting in the Babatag Range and survival in Turkey to the early 1990s; other sources say 1957-1968. 1970 (Hakkari, Turkey) is one disputed date.
Last confirmed record 1976 at Meru Betiri (tracks; no confirmed sightings after 1979); IUCN extinct 2003.
Last bird (Orange Band) died 17 June 1987.
Last seen 1989 in Monteverde, Costa Rica.
Celia found dead under a fallen tree 6 Jan 2000; a clone was born in 2003 and died within minutes.
Six-week Yangtze survey in late 2006 found none; announced December 2006 (some sources say declared 2007).
Died 24 June 2012.

US Fish and Wildlife Service proposed delisting the ivory-billed woodpecker as extinct, with 22 other species, announced 29-30 Sept 2021; not finalized as of 2023. Last widely accepted sighting 2004 in Arkansas; some researchers dispute the conclusion. Name and description are consistent and state no date.
IUCN Red List update July 2022 declared it extinct; last confirmed sighting 2003.
